newsitem.title: UK: Wm Cook calls for Triplex bid rejection.
newsitem.headline: Wm Cook calls for Triplex bid rejection.

text.p: British steel firm William Cook appealed again to its shareholders to reject efforts by engineering group Triplex Lloyd to take it over, saying the bid defied industrial logic.
William Cook faces a hotile bid from Triplex Lloyd which values Cook at about 309 pence per share, lower than its 357-1/2p share price at the market close on Friday.
Cook said Triplex Lloyd would not be able to effect any significant synergies or savings after the takeover.

"Only six percent of William Cook's turnover is produced from similar processes and for similar markets as those in which Triplex Lloyd is principally involved," it said. "Claims that there can be significant manufacturing synergies are therefore without foundation."
Triplex said last week that it was extending the bid to 1500 GMT on Janury 14 after it had received acceptances for about 5.83 percent of Cook's ordinary share capital by December 31.
Cook said it did not see any purchasing synergies either, with its primary raw material being steel scrap against Triplex's main purchases of iron and ceramics.
Cook also criticised Triplex's management, casting doubts on its "ability to manage effectively a business like William Cook".
The target firm pointed out that Triplex Lloyd had suffered losses in three out of the last six years.
Andrew Cook, the chairman of William Cook, said the bid was clearly "not in the interest of shareholders of either company".
